references.authors: March, J. G.
references.title: Exploration and Exploitation in Organizational Learning
references.note: Foundational treatment of discovering alternatives versus refining existing knowledge. Directly relevant mechanism; organizational learning, not human lifestyle categories.

references.authors: Smaldino, P. E., Moser, C., Perez Velilla, A., & Werling, M.
references.title: Maintaining Transient Diversity Is a General Principle for Improving Collective Problem Solving
references.note: Unifies diverse mechanisms that prevent premature convergence. Useful overview of conditions and tradeoffs; not a meta-analysis of societal personality composition.

references.authors: Taylor, H., Fernandes, B., & Wraight, S.
references.title: The Evolution of Complementary Cognition: Humans Cooperatively Adapt and Evolve through a System of Collective Cognitive Search
references.note: Proposes complementary specializations in human cognitive search. A close conceptual match whose evolutionary and contemporary implications require further testing.

references.authors: Pringle, T. A., & Robinson, M. D.
references.title: The diversity advantage: An explanatory framework for personality traits
references.note: Proposes that personality variation contributes to collective cognition and group processes. This is one possible explanatory framework, not settled evidence about why personality evolved.

references.authors: Pringle, T. A., Stramer, L., & Robinson, M. D.
references.title: Bounded personality diversity boosts collective intelligence: a swarm optimization approach
references.note: Compares agent compositions across 11 mathematical landscapes. Personality is approximated through limited algorithmic parameters; real human validation is explicitly outstanding.

references.authors: Grajzel, K., Acar, S., & Singer, G.
references.title: The Big Five and divergent thinking: A meta-analysis
references.note: 63 studies and 24,298 participants; a modest openness-divergent thinking association. Creative potential and consequential innovation remain different outcomes.

references.authors: Feist, G. J.
references.title: A meta-analysis of personality in scientific and artistic creativity
references.note: Classic evidence linking creativity with unconventionality and openness, alongside drive and ambition. Occupational comparisons and heterogeneity limit causal interpretation.

references.authors: Stanek, K. C., & Ones, D. S.
references.title: Meta-analytic relations between personality and cognitive ability
references.note: Distinguishes broad traits, aspects and facets. Industriousness relates positively to originality/creativity ability, illustrating the limits of an order-versus-creativity dichotomy.

references.authors: Wilson, R. C., Geana, A., White, J. M., Ludvig, E. A., & Cohen, J. D.
references.title: Humans use directed and random exploration to solve the explore-exploit dilemma
references.note: Separates information-seeking and choice variability in 30 participants. Evidence about how exploration is deployed; random noise was not optimal in this task's normative model.

references.authors: Cheng, C., Lau, H.-P. B., & Chan, M.-P. S.
references.title: Coping flexibility and psychological adjustment to stressful life changes: A meta-analytic review
references.note: 58,946 participants; situation-sensitive adaptation shows stronger associations than variability alone. Individual adjustment, not social innovation, is the outcome.

references.authors: Riddell, H., et al.
references.title: A meta-analytic review and conceptual model of the antecedents and outcomes of goal adjustment in response to striving difficulties
references.note: 235 studies; distinguishes disengagement, reengagement and flexibility. Authors rate accumulated evidence low to moderate because of design, heterogeneity and publication-bias limitations.

references.authors: Aeon, B., Faber, A., & Panaccio, A.
references.title: Does time management work? A meta-analysis
references.note: 158 studies; positive relationships with performance and wellbeing. Time management includes adaptation, and much of the evidence is correlational.

references.authors: Moffitt, T. E., et al.
references.title: A gradient of childhood self-control predicts health, wealth, and public safety
references.note: Birth-cohort and sibling evidence links self-control with later life outcomes. Useful counterweight to conflating exploration with poor regulation; causality is not experimentally established.

references.authors: Mitchell, K. E., Levin, A. S., & Krumboltz, J. D.
references.title: Planned Happenstance: Constructing Unexpected Career Opportunities
references.note: Frames chance events as opportunities that active exploration can help create and use. Conceptual foundation, not a comparative trial of planned versus unplanned lives.

references.authors: Kim, B., et al.
references.title: Longitudinal Relationships Between Planned Happenstance Skills and Life Adjustment and the Moderating Role of Career Barriers
references.note: 307 Korean students during school-to-work transition. A bundled set of happenstance skills preceded adjustment; contextual and causal limits remain.

references.authors: Pryor, R. G. L., & Bright, J.
references.title: The Chaos Theory of Careers
references.note: Emphasizes complexity, chance and nonlinear changes in careers. The term chaos describes career dynamics, rather than a validated personality category.

references.authors: Tonietto, G. N., & Malkoc, S. A.
references.title: The Calendar Mindset: Scheduling Takes the Fun Out and Puts the Work In
references.note: 13 studies identify costs of precise scheduling for leisure enjoyment, removed by rough scheduling. Directly relevant to everyday spontaneity but narrow in scope.

references.authors: Sio, U. N., & Ormerod, T. C.
references.title: Does incubation enhance problem solving? A meta-analytic review
references.note: Supports setting a problem aside before returning, with important task and break moderators. Concerns alternating activities rather than a fixed personality.

references.authors: Sarasvathy, S. D.
references.title: Causation and Effectuation: Toward a Theoretical Shift from Economic Inevitability to Entrepreneurial Contingency
references.note: Contrasts prediction-led reasoning with constructing possibilities from available means. Effectuation is active and resource-aware, not passive drift.

references.authors: Brinckmann, J., Grichnik, D., & Kapsa, D.
references.title: Should entrepreneurs plan or just storm the castle? A meta-analysis on contextual factors impacting the business planning-performance relationship in small firms
references.note: 46 studies; positive average planning-performance relationship with context dependence. The authors recommend a dynamic combination of planning and learning.

references.authors: Smolka, K. M., Verheul, I., Burmeister-Lamp, K., & Heugens, P. P. M. A. R.
references.title: Get It Together! Synergistic Effects of Causal and Effectual Decision-Making Logics on Venture Performance
references.note: 1,453 entrepreneurs in 25 countries; combined approaches associated with better performance. This DOI is the retained publication, rather than its withdrawn duplicate.

references.authors: Junni, P., Sarala, R. M., Taras, V., & Tarba, S. Y.
references.title: Organizational Ambidexterity and Performance: A Meta-Analysis
references.note: Combining exploratory and exploitative activities is associated with performance, moderated by setting and methodology. Does not determine a personality mix.

references.authors: Konradt, U., Nath, A., & Oldeweme, M.
references.title: Planning and Performance in Teams: A Bayesian Meta-Analytic Structural Equation Modeling Approach
references.note: 33 samples and 1,885 teams; moderate positive planning-performance association. Planning quality is more informative than quantity; long-term evidence is limited.

references.authors: Peeters, M. A. G., van Tuijl, H. F. J. M., Rutte, C. G., & Reymen, I. M. M. J.
references.title: Personality and Team Performance: A Meta-Analysis
references.note: Mean conscientiousness is positively associated with team performance; within-team variation is negatively associated. A direct caution against treating all personality diversity as beneficial.

references.authors: Jolic Marjanovic, Z., et al.
references.title: The Big Five and Collaborative Problem Solving: A Narrative Systematic Review
references.note: 47 papers; conscientiousness and agreeableness support different aspects of collaboration. Aggregation methods and levels of analysis affect conclusions.

references.authors: De Dreu, C. K. W., & West, M. A.
references.title: Minority Dissent and Team Innovation: The Importance of Participation in Decision Making
references.note: Dissent was associated with innovation when participation was high. The capacity to consider different ideas conditions their value.

references.authors: Nemeth, C., Brown, K., & Rogers, J.
references.title: Devil's Advocate versus Authentic Dissent: Stimulating Quantity and Quality
references.note: Authentic dissent stimulated better solutions than assigned disagreement. Relevant to independent perspectives; not an endorsement of arbitrary conflict.

references.authors: de Wit, F. R. C., Greer, L. L., & Jehn, K. A.
references.title: The Paradox of Intragroup Conflict: A Meta-Analysis
references.note: 116 studies and 8,880 groups; interpersonal/process conflict show negative relationships, while task disagreement has more conditional effects.

references.authors: Shirado, H., & Christakis, N. A.
references.title: Locally noisy autonomous agents improve global human coordination in network experiments
references.note: Small, centrally placed behavioral noise improved a coordination game. The manipulated actors were bots; the effective noise level and network location were task-specific.

references.authors: Bernstein, E., Shore, J., & Lazer, D.
references.title: How intermittent breaks in interaction improve collective intelligence
references.note: Alternating independent search with social influence combined strong average and best-solution performance. A temporal alternative to permanent personality roles.

references.authors: Hong, L., & Page, S. E.
references.title: Groups of diverse problem solvers can outperform groups of high-ability problem solvers
references.note: Functional diversity can overcome correlated blind spots under specified conditions. This is neither an unconditional theorem about diversity nor a real-person composition experiment.

references.authors: Mason, W., & Watts, D. J.
references.title: Collaborative learning in networks
references.note: 256 experiments; efficient networks outperformed inefficient ones, challenging simple diffusion models. Participants adjusted their exploration to context.

references.authors: Derex, M., & Boyd, R.
references.title: Partial connectivity increases cultural accumulation within groups
references.note: Partially connected groups preserved distinct trajectories needed for recombinant innovation. The artificial task's structure is an important boundary condition.

references.authors: Deffner, D., et al.
references.title: Collective incentives reduce over-exploitation of social information in unconstrained human groups
references.note: Copying can yield individual gains and group losses under concentrated resources. Collective incentives changed information use and adaptation.

references.authors: Chirkov, V., Kurvers, R. H. J. M., Romanczuk, P., & Deffner, D.
references.title: Payoff selectivity drives collective intelligence during dynamic resource tracking in humans
references.note: 621 participants; continuous payoff visibility enabled a group advantage over solitary search. Social information without quality cues did not reliably help.

references.authors: Bolton, P., & Harris, C.
references.title: Strategic Experimentation
references.note: Experimentation creates information with benefits beyond the experimenter. Models the resulting strategic incentives and gap from socially optimal learning.

references.authors: Azoulay, P., Graff Zivin, J. S., & Manso, G.
references.title: Incentives and Creativity: Evidence from the Academic Life Sciences
references.note: Funding systems that allow freedom and early failure were associated with more high-impact and exploratory research. Matching and longitudinal methods reduce but cannot eliminate selection concerns.

references.authors: Burt, R. S.
references.title: Structural Holes and Good Ideas
references.note: Bridging otherwise separated groups is associated with valuable ideas. Provides an information-access mechanism rather than a personality-based randomness account.

references.authors: Chua, R. Y. J., Roth, Y., & Lemoine, J.-F.
references.title: The Impact of Culture on Creativity: How Cultural Tightness and Cultural Distance Affect Global Innovation Crowdsourcing Work
references.note: Tightness has different relationships with creative work in familiar and distant cultural contexts. Evidence about norms and audiences, not lifetime planning.

references.authors: Uzzi, B., Mukherjee, S., Stringer, M., & Jones, B.
references.title: Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact
references.note: 17.9 million papers; high impact associates with conventional foundations plus unusual combinations. Citation impact is not equivalent to social welfare.

references.authors: Wu, L., Wang, D., & Evans, J. A.
references.title: Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology
references.note: Team size relates to developing versus disrupting knowledge trajectories. Institutional arrangements can shape contribution without a fixed personality explanation.

references.authors: Wolf, M., van Doorn, G. S., & Weissing, F. J.
references.title: Evolutionary emergence of responsive and unresponsive personalities
references.note: Frequency-dependent benefits and experience-dependent costs produce persistent responsiveness differences. Evolutionary fitness does not establish societal welfare maximization.

references.authors: Liang, Z. S., et al.
references.title: Molecular determinants of scouting behavior in honey bees
references.note: Consistent exploratory tendencies across contexts, with molecular and neurochemical correlates. Biological analogy rather than evidence about human nonplanners.

references.authors: Rendell, L., et al.
references.title: Why Copy Others? Insights from the Social Learning Strategies Tournament
references.note: Social learning performs well because observed behavior is already filtered by others' experience. Relative strategy success depends on the tournament rules.

references.authors: Gopnik, A., et al.
references.title: Changes in cognitive flexibility and hypothesis search across human life history from childhood to adolescence to adulthood
references.note: Examines age-related hypothesis search in physical and social domains. Suggests life-stage allocation as an alternative to fixed adult explorer and planner types.

references.authors: Zollman, K. J. S.
references.title: The Epistemic Benefit of Transient Diversity
references.note: Maintaining alternative research directions can avoid premature consensus; persistent fragmentation can also prevent learning. Benefits concern temporary, useful diversity.

references.authors: Wu, J., & O'Connor, C.
references.title: How should we promote transient diversity in science?
references.note: Evaluates ways to protect diverse scientific practice while accounting for costs, feasibility, and ethics. Helpful bridge from models to institutional proposals.

references.authors: Aggarwal, I., Woolley, A. W., Chabris, C. F., & Malone, T. W.
references.title: The Impact of Cognitive Style Diversity on Implicit Learning in Teams
references.note: 98 teams; an inverted-U association between cognitive-style diversity and collective intelligence. The styles are not planning/spontaneity, and composition was not randomly manipulated.

references.authors: Nettle, D.
references.title: The evolution of personality variation in humans and other animals
references.note: Personality dimensions can involve different fitness costs and benefits. Provides an alternative to assuming that variation exists for collective social advantage.

references.authors: Davis, J. P., Eisenhardt, K. M., & Bingham, C. B.
references.title: Optimal Structure, Market Dynamism, and the Strategy of Simple Rules
references.note: Examines the costs of too much and too little structure as environments change. Conclusions depend on the modeled tasks and organizational assumptions.

references.authors: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P.
references.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-Analysis of Effects and Processes
references.note: Classic synthesis of 94 tests of concrete if-then action plans. Supports goal execution, which is distinct from committing to an inflexible lifelong plan.
